If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If forecast deviates >1.5% from true value in mid-horizon (8–15 days), adjust forecast by +0.3–0.7% if sentiment is positive, or -0.3–0.7% if sentiment is negative, to align with sentiment bias.

If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent momentum overcorrection.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to avoid overestimating continuation.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon to avoid premature reversal.
